title: Prompt replay & stochastic-variance log
content:
Purpose:
Capture ad-hoc findings from replaying prompts across stochastic seeds / temperatures and documenting failure modes. This is a personal lab log — rough, iterative. Use for checklist before formalizing into a runbook.

Goals:
- Understand how much surface-level output variance affects downstream QA metrics (intent classification, slot fill, extractive QA).
- Identify which prompt structures are brittle vs stable under sampling (temp > 0).
- Prototype lightweight replay metadata to store with responses (seed, rng-state, prefix-hash, model-variant).

Quick takeaways so far:
- Deterministic decoding (top_k=1 / temp=0) hides many hallucination classes but increases repetition; not always acceptable for UX.
- Few-shot exemplars with explicit outcome schema are much more stable than unconstrained freeform shots.
- Short system instructions + long user examples tend to increase variance (apparently examples dominate the context distribution).

Experiment design (ad-hoc):
- Model: redwood/rlhf-mini-v2 (dev cluster)
- Prompts: 12 canonical prompts (3 categories: summarization, slot extraction, persona reply)
- Seeds: 12 different RNG seeds per prompt + deterministic run
- Sampling configs: temp=0, 0.3, 0.7; top_p=0.95 default; also test top_k=40 vs top_k=1
- Logging: store prompt hash, model, seed, token-level probs (summary), latency, tokens_out, and returned text.

Example prompt set (summarization; few-shot 2-shot):
SYSTEM: You are a terse summarizer. Output one-sentence summary, do not add opinion.
SHOT1 (input -> output):
Input: "Company X raised $40M to build infra for inference"
Output: "Company X raised $40M to fund inference infrastructure."
SHOT2 (input -> output):
Input: "New research shows quantized transformers are 2x faster"
Output: "Research demonstrates quantized transformers yield 2x speedups."
USER: "Write a one-sentence summary for: \"Redwood launched a dedicated offering for private deployments.\""

Observed outputs (temp=0.3, three seeds):
- seed A: "Redwood launched a dedicated offering enabling private deployments for customers." (passes schema)
- seed B: "Redwood introduced Dedicated, a new offering for private and on-premise deployments aimed at regulated customers." (passes schema, more detail)
- seed C: "Redwood launched Dedicated to help customers run inference in private environments." (passes but different word choice)

Failure case snapshot (slot extraction):
Prompt: extract "start_date" from natural language onboarding notes. Shot examples used loosely formatted dates.
- Many runs returned relative dates ("two weeks ago") instead of canonical ISO.
- Deterministic run returned blank when anchor phrase missing.

Hypotheses / notes:
- Few-shot exemplars with canonicalized outputs help conversion to ISO: include one negative example ("no date present -> null").
- When user input is noisy, prefer an explicit normalization step (call a small extraction model) before generation.
- Store and surface RNG seed to SRE/ops to aid debug: add header in response metadata (x-replay-seed).

Evaluation heuristics to add to harness:
- Jaccard/Averaged-BLEU for summarization stability across seeds
- Slot F1 aggregated with a majority-vote baseline
- Semantic similarity (embedding cosine) to exemplar outputs to detect drift

Small experiments to run next week:
- Swap exemplar order (shot1 vs shot2) and measure variance delta (quick hypothesis: order matters strongly for temp>0).
- Test a micro-cache: if prompt hash + exemplar order seen before, return cached answer for temp>0 runs until TTL expired. Measure UX delta.
- Add a schema-enforcer prompt post-processing instruction ("Return strictly JSON object with keys: ...") and compare parsing errors.

Open questions / TODOs:
- What minimum metadata do we store to support reproducible bug reports without leaking PII? (seed, model-variant, prompt-hash OK; full prompt maybe redacted).
- Where to land replay logs at scale? (S3 vs dedicated db vs tracing pipeline). Cost/retention tradeoffs.
- Should replay integration be opt-in or default for Dedicated tenants? Data residency concerns.

Scratch ideas (very rough):
- "Prompt zipper" — append a 32-byte stable context fingerprint that models as an anchor token; helps ensure same prefix encoding across clients.
- Seed-aware playground: a UI slider to step seeds and see differences live; useful during prompt tuning sessions.

Link to my ephemeral notebook for outputs: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-dev-replay/scratch/maya/replay-samples-20250304.json (internal)

Notes-to-self: capture a 1-paragraph summary of this doc for Confluence, include a small matrix: (prompt-type x temp) -> variance score. If Rafael agrees, spin up a 1-day infra spike to implement seed header + minimal S3 persist.

-- Maya
